title: asyncio.run(main()) runs on import
detail: Importing run_scraper triggers a full LinkedIn scrape because the call sits at module top level with no `if __name__ == '__main__':` guard. Any tool that auto-imports modules (linters, tests) launches Playwright and scrapes the feed.

title: github_trigger.py imports `requests` but it isn't in requirements.txt
detail: Either add `requests>=2.31` to requirements.txt or migrate to `httpx` (already pulled in by fastapi).

title: `send_referral_email` called with empty string for `to_email`
detail: step.run("send-email", send_referral_email, "", name, company, target_role) — to_email is always "". In DRY_RUN it silently prints success; in production the SMTP call goes to an empty address and raises (or sends to nobody). The campaign target's email is never resolved/stored anywhere.

title: Package `mailer.email` shadows stdlib `email`
detail: The file does `from email.mime.text import MIMEText`, which works because absolute imports take precedence — but anywhere a relative resolver kicks in (some test runners, deps using __import__('email')) you'd get the local file instead of stdlib email. Rename to `mailer/mailer.py` or `mailer/smtp.py`.

title: `datetime.utcnow()` deprecated in Python 3.12+; removed in 3.14
detail: Files: ['main.py', 'agents/auto_apply.py', 'agents/connection.py', 'agents/content.py', 'agents/feed_scout.py', 'agents/job_hunter.py', 'agents/referral.py', 'browser/easy_apply.py', 'core/action_queue.py', 'core/budget.py']…. Replace with `datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc)` (or use `datetime.UTC` on 3.11+).

title: int(os.getenv('APPLICANT_YOE','2')) raises on empty string env var
detail: If APPLICANT_YOE='' is in the environment (common Docker/CI footgun) the default never kicks in and int('') raises ValueError at module import time. Same risk on WARMUP_WEEK, AUTO_REPOST_THRESHOLD, CONNECTION_THRESHOLD, JOB_SLACK_THRESHOLD.

title: Inner shadow import of `re` via __import__('re')
detail: Module already does `import re` at line 1. The local `import_re = __import__('re')` inside `_extract_content` is dead/redundant — drop it.

title: AsyncIOMotorClient instantiated at import time
detail: Doesn't fail at import (it's lazy until first I/O), but means tools that import the package eagerly will hold an open client handle that they never close. Consider lazy-construction inside a `get_db()` helper.

title: `modal if True else None` is dead-code conditional
detail: The expression always evaluates to `modal`. Simplify to `await _dismiss_modal(page, modal)` or remove the `True` placeholder.

title: `modal.page` access on Playwright 1.44 — Locator has no `.page` attribute
detail: In `_handle_resume`, `modal` is a `Locator`. Playwright Python only added the `Locator.page` property in 1.46+; requirements pin to 1.44.*. This raises AttributeError the first time a resume upload runs. Pass `page` in instead.

title: Type hint `auto_resume_hours: int = None` mismatches default
detail: Should be `Optional[int] = None` or `int | None = None` to satisfy strict type checkers (mypy / pyright).

title: Boolean profile fields stored as strings
detail: willing_to_relocate / requires_sponsorship are kept as the raw env string (e.g. 'false'). Downstream llm.service.answer_application_question feeds them into a prompt as-is; that works, but you'll trip if anything compares `profile['requires_sponsorship'] is True`.

title: .jobs-search-results-list selector is stale on new LinkedIn layout
detail: The 2025/2026 jobs page uses `.scaffold-layout__list-container ul` instead. As coded, `await page.locator('.jobs-search-results-list').click()` throws and the next 3 PageDown presses never fire, so jobs are not scrolled into view. scrape_jobs typically returns the first ~6 cards only.

title: `li.reusable-search__result-container` selector is stale
detail: New LinkedIn people search uses `div[data-chameleon-result-urn]` (or the generic `li[componentkey]`). This selector returns 0 elements; `search_people` then returns [].

title: Synchronous LLM/Groq calls run inside async coroutines → blocks event loop
detail: score_connection_profile / generate_connection_note / score_job_post / score_post_for_repost / classify_feed_post_as_job / generate_engage_comment are all sync `def`s. Each call to Groq's REST API blocks the asyncio loop for the request's duration (~200-800ms). For large fan-outs this serializes work and stalls anything else (e.g. concurrent scrapes). Wrap with `await asyncio.to_thread(...)` or use the async Groq client.

title: Top-level `asyncio.run(main())` with no __main__ guard
detail: Importing test_connect_manual.py (which any test discovery / static analyzer will do) triggers a real LinkedIn session. Wrap in `if __name__ == '__main__': asyncio.run(main())`.

title: Top-level `asyncio.run(main())` with no __main__ guard
detail: Importing test_feed_scout.py (which any test discovery / static analyzer will do) triggers a real LinkedIn session. Wrap in `if __name__ == '__main__': asyncio.run(main())`.

title: Top-level `asyncio.run(main())` with no __main__ guard
detail: Importing test_recent_jobs.py (which any test discovery / static analyzer will do) triggers a real LinkedIn session. Wrap in `if __name__ == '__main__': asyncio.run(main())`.

title: Per-profile work isn't wrapped in `step.run` — Inngest retries duplicate side effects
detail: The for-loop calls `db.connections.update_one(... upsert=True)` and `ActionQueue.push(...)` directly. If the function fails after queuing some but not all profiles, Inngest retries from the top — those already-queued profiles will be queued AGAIN (upsert skips DB dup, but ActionQueue has no idempotency key). Move each profile's mutations under `step.run('process-' + url, ...)`.

title: Resume upload step silently returns when file missing
detail: If APPLICANT_RESUME_PATH points at a non-existent file, `_handle_resume` no-ops. The Easy Apply walker then advances to the next step thinking the upload succeeded, often hitting a backend validation failure that wastes an application slot. Either raise a needs_human signal here or pre-validate the resume on startup.
